splashes: She is watching you read this.
Gods have no hands, only Laws.
Every gift has a second line.
You died. It went quite well.
The Demon Lord cannot be hurt. Yet.
One dragon. Only one. Please do not wake it.
Now with fewer gods touching things.
Read the small print on your Laws.
There is a stone with your name on it, nearly.
Nobody can make you pray. She can only ask.
A crown is only a heavy hat with a Law on it.
tips: A lamp keeps the dark things from rising near it. Light your door before you sleep.
You can fall five blocks unhurt, and any distance at all into water.
The right tool cuts the time a block takes. A block above your tool's level takes far longer and gives you nothing.
Recipes open by themselves once you have held what goes into them.
Press {pray} anywhere to pray. A full Faith bar is a Law she owes you.
Every Law has a gift and a price. Which you take is how you choose how hard the world is.
You may ask her for other words once for each Law.
A Law Stone adds a fourth card to what she offers.
Dying drops nothing. It only costs you your run of nights.
A staff in the hand strengthens every spell you cast.
Pick your two spells in the bag. {spell1} and {spell2} cast them.
Throw things with {drop}, and the whole stack with Ctrl. Anything thrown near a Law Stone is an offering.
Whatever the bag has no room for stays on the ground. Nothing is lost.
Crossings on the Old Ways have chests that stock themselves the first time they are opened.
The guild in any city has a board of quests.
News travels at walking pace. The next town has not heard what you did yet.
A witness runs to the law. Crime is much cheaper with nobody watching.
When you pause, the whole world waits. Nothing happens behind your back.
Marks on the compass follow whoever you are after, even when they move.

guide.title: Your story
text: You died on Earth. A god met you in the heavens and sent you down with one job: end the Demon Lord.
The god cannot touch the world. Gods have no hands, only Laws. She can say a thing out loud and the world will enforce it, and every gift she writes comes with a price.
The journal ({journal}) always says what to do next, and the compass and the map ({map}) show where.

guide.title: Moving
text: You can step up one block without jumping, fall five blocks unhurt, and fall any distance into water.
Ropes and ladders hold you. Climb them with {forward} and {back}.

guide.title: Fighting
text: Left click strikes. Right click uses what is in your hand, so a shield rises and a bow draws for as long as you hold it.
{spell1} and {spell2} cast the two spells you have chosen in the bag. A staff in the hand strengthens them.
Kills in a row build a chain, and each one rings higher than the last. Lamps keep monsters away, and they come out in the dark.

guide.title: Gathering and making
text: Hold left click to mine. What breaks pops out and lands, and you take it by walking over it. If the bag is full it waits on the ground.
Each block wants a tool. The right one is much faster, and a block above your tool's level takes far longer and gives nothing.
The first nine slots of the bag ({bag}) are your hotbar. Recipes open once you have held what goes into them, and tables, furnaces and forges open bigger ones.

guide.title: People and the law
text: {talk} talks or trades with whoever is near. People remember what you did, and news reaches other towns at walking pace.
A crime with a witness puts a bounty on you and sends hunters after you. Crime with nobody watching is a quieter matter.
The guild in any city has a board of quests, and anyone may ask you a favor.

guide.title: Faith and Laws
text: Every deed fills the Faith bar on your dock. A full bar is a little more health and a Law she owes you.
Press {pray} to pray. She offers three Laws, each with a gift and a price, and you choose one. That choice is how you set how hard the world is.
The world can hold only three of her Laws, so a fourth pushes out the oldest. Asking for one you already hold deepens it: the gift grows and the price does not.
An offering is whatever you hold while you pray, or anything thrown down near a Law Stone.

guide.title: Death and rest
text: Dying drops nothing and costs no Faith. It only ends your run of nights survived.
A night at an inn is safe, and sometimes it brings a dream.
The world saves by itself, and when you pause everything waits. Sieges, festivals and raids run on time played, so nothing can happen while you are away.

guide.title: All the keys
text: Every key here can be changed in Options, under Controls.

credits.title: Crown Reborn
lines: The story, the people and every line they say are written and shipped with the game. Nothing here needs an AI service, an account or a key.
